2607.27134.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
2607.27134.paper_summary: Writing and communication are increasingly mediated by large language models (LLMs) that are being used to draft, revise and polish text. Although such assistance can improve clarity and help authors meet institutional expectations, widespread reliance on shared models may reduce population-level variation in linguistic form, a phenomenon we refer to as linguistic monoculture. We develop a mathematical framework in which authors and LLMs are represented as distributions over linguistic features and coevolve through repeated interaction. We analyze three interaction mechanisms: a shared model with a fixed linguistic distribution, a shared model recursively updated from author outputs, and personalized models updated through author-specific and population-level feedback. We characterize the resulting equilibria and convergence rates, showing that, shared models can drive authors toward a common norm, recursive feedback relocates the shared norm without altering pairwise spread under common conformity, and personalization can preserve a family of distinct author-model equilibria with nonzero linguistic diversity. We then endogenize conformity as a strategic choice trading off private benefits from clarity, legibility, and perceived fluency against distinctive style. Within this utility model, individually rational authors may conform more than is socially optimal because they do not internalize the value their distinctiveness provides to others, creating a negative externality and a price of monoculture that is finite for each fixed instance but can grow without bound when distinctiveness dominates authenticity. Synthetic simulations illustrate how fixed shared assistance, recursive feedback, and personalization produce different long-run diversity outcomes.
2607.27134.paper_summary_zh: 寫作和交流越來越多地受到大型語言模型（LLMs）的媒介，這些模型被用來草擬、修訂和潤飾文本。雖然這種協助可以提高清晰度並幫助作者滿足機構期望，但對共享模型的廣泛依賴可能會降低語言形式的群體層面變異性，這種現象我們稱之為語言單一文化。我們發展了一個數學框架，在這個框架中，作者和LLMs被表示為語言特徵的分佈，並通過重複互動共同演化。我們分析了三種互動機制：具有固定語言分佈的共享模型、從作者輸出中遞歸更新的共享模型，以及通過作者特定和群體層面反饋更新的個性化模型。我們描述了由此產生的均衡和收斂速率，顯示共享模型可以將作者推向共同的規範，遞歸反饋在不改變在共同遵從下的成對擴散的情況下重新定位共享規範，而個性化可以保留一系列具有非零語言多樣性的獨特作者-模型均衡。然後，我們將遵從內生化為一種戰略選擇，權衡來自清晰度、可讀性和感知流暢性的私人利益與獨特風格之間的取捨。在這個效用模型中，個別理性的作者可能會比社會最優狀況下更遵從，因為他們沒有內部化他們的獨特性對他人的價值，從而造成負外部性和一種單一文化的代價，這在每個固定實例中是有限的，但當獨特性主導真實性時，可以無限增長。合成模擬展示了固定共享協助、遞歸反饋和個性化如何產生不同的長期多樣性結果。
